name: Leucine supplements
short: Acute studies in men: blood ammonia above normal at very high leucine intakes; long-term studies needed. Leucine-rich amino acid mix in 55 older CKD patients: no significant adverse event difference.
text: A review of leucine safety describes acute diet studies in young men, in whom blood ammonia rose above normal values at the leucine-oxidation breakpoint of 550 mg per kg per day, and in elderly men (about 72 years old), in whom blood ammonia was above normal at intakes above 550 mg per kg per day; the authors note these were acute studies and that longer-term studies are needed. A second review states that very few studies have sought the maximum safe intake and that, on limited evidence, the intakes studied did not appear to have health consequences other than short-term rises in plasma ammonia; it calls for research on leucine toxicity in the elderly and in specific health conditions. A broader review of amino acid supplements, which included leucine, concluded that enhanced intake of most amino acid supplements may not be risk-free and can cause a number of detrimental side effects; its abstract does not say which harms apply to leucine. In a 12-week randomised placebo-controlled trial in 55 people over 65 with chronic kidney disease, adverse events did not differ significantly between a leucine-enriched branched-chain amino acid mixture taken by mouth and placebo. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
